canonicality.rule: This file is the single source of truth for every value in this package. docs/FORESEAL_BILATERAL_TERMS_V1_1.md and manifest/manifest.md are generated from it or checked against it by tools/check-consistency.cjs. If any human-readable document disagrees with this file, this file wins and the disagreement is a defect.
canonicality.why_this_rule_exists: At tag foreseal-bilateral-v1 the human terms and this manifest disagreed materially on the bond wallet, the funding status, the custody model and the slash-execution path. A provenance package whose own machine-readable record contradicts its prose has no business asking anyone to trust its receipts. See SUPERSESSION.json for the full list.

identification.why_not_quoted: A document cannot contain its own commit hash, and the v1 attempt to quote one in prose is exactly how v1 shipped wrong: its Parties table claimed the tag resolved to cd0c3f630f92… while the tag actually resolved to c68e06aa2d69…. This package therefore never quotes its own SHA. Resolve the tag, and verify content with the per-file checksums below, which are self-verifying and independent of any commit hash.

immutability.claim: The versioned tag identifies the release; the resolved commit SHA is the immutable object being reviewed.
immutability.disclosure: This repository has zero rulesets and no branch/tag protection (verifiable: GET /repos/stillmarcus24/notary-x402-reference-kit/rulesets returns []). A git tag is therefore movable by anyone with write access. Tag foreseal-bilateral-v1 said 'A tag, not a branch head, so it cannot drift' — that was an overclaim and is retracted. The durable identifier is the commit SHA you resolve, plus the checksums below. Record the SHA when you resolve it; do not rely on the tag alone.

success_criterion._correction_2026_09_11: Tag foreseal-bilateral-v1 asserted, in both this manifest and the human terms, that 'A REJECTED terminal state is a successful, valid test outcome' and that 'Neither party will characterize a REJECTED outcome as a failed test.' success_criterion.bilateral: Both parties execute the frozen lifecycle below, independently verify the resulting artifacts, and publish their observations and any divergences. No terminal outcome is pre-agreed by either party.

stillos_local_expectation.expectation: Because the reference fact is permanently true, StillOS expects the dispute re-run to agree with the original verdict and therefore to terminate REJECTED.
stillos_local_expectation.status: This is StillOS's own prediction, recorded in advance so it can be checked against the result. It is not a bilateral agreement, it is not binding on ForeSeal, and ForeSeal is free to characterize any outcome however its own review supports.

lifecycle_steps.action: ForeSeal calls POST /claim-verdict from a ForeSeal-controlled wallet, paying the x402-quoted price, with the resolver spec above.
lifecycle_steps.must_not_use: The free tier does not return a verdict_receipt hash/signature to the caller and is NOT usable for this test — confirmed live 2026-09-06 (signed:false, verdict_receipt:null on the free path).

lifecycle_steps.action: StillOS returns a signed, hash-chained claim receipt AND a signed, hash-chained verdict receipt, both bound to the resolver above.
StillOS resolves the claim against api.github.com in real time and posts the verdict inline in the same response.
ForeSeal verifies the verdict receipt OFFLINE: recompute receipt_hash, resolve notary_fp against the PINNED key/keyring in keys/, verify Ed25519 signature, confirm chain to prior receipt.

ForeSeal files POST /dispute with receipt_hash + the exact verdict_object it received + the same resolver spec + counter-evidence/reason. Optionally supplies disputant_wallet, the 0x address any payout would be sent to.
verdict_dispute.cjs re-runs the SAME resolver spec fresh, right now, and compares the fresh label to the original verdict label. The terminal state is whatever that comparison produces.
lifecycle_steps.stillos_expected_result: REJECTED — see success_criterion.stillos_local_expectation. Not pre-agreed by ForeSeal.

lifecycle_steps.action: IF the dispute is UPHELD, a payout obligation is recorded durably and synchronously before any signature is sought or any alert is sent. See payout_obligation below. Payment itself requires a human 2-of-2 Safe signature and is never automatic.

dispute_semantics.hash_binding: The disputer must supply the exact verdict_object they were given; it is checked against the receipt's committed claim_sha256 before anything else runs — a fabricated verdict_object is rejected before any write.
dispute_semantics.target_mutation_guard: The fresh re-run's settles_against must equal the original verdict's settles_against, or the dispute is rejected — a disputer cannot swap in an easier target.
dispute_semantics.indeterminate_guard: If the resolver cannot reach its source, the dispute returns INDETERMINATE and is retryable. An unreachable source never counts as a refutation and never reserves a dispute_id.
dispute_semantics.dispute_window: 48 hours from the original verdict receipt's timestamp.
dispute_semantics.dedup: A deterministic dispute_id derived from protocol version, disputed receipt hash, committed claim hash, normalized challenger and normalized counter-evidence digest. A duplicate produces no second receipt and no second obligation.

payout_obligation._added_2026_09_11: Answers the question 0rkz asked on x402#2887: what happens to a claim while it waits for the second signature. At tag foreseal-bilateral-v1 the answer was: nothing durable. The slash directive was an in-memory object returned in the HTTP response plus a best-effort alert in a swallowed try/catch; it was never persisted, and the live /dispute handler did not even forward it to the caller. Under 2-of-2 custody that interval is unbounded, so the debt is now written down before anything else happens.
payout_obligation.opened_when: Synchronously inside the dispute request, immediately on an UPHELD adjudication — before the reputation write, before the founder alert, before any signature is sought. Deliberately not wrapped in a try/catch: if the obligation cannot be recorded, the request fails loudly rather than returning a successful-looking overturn with no record of the debt.
payout_obligation.ledger: state/proof-notary/slash-obligations.jsonl — append-only, hash-chained, tamper-evident. Current state is a fold over events, never a mutable field.
payout_obligation.overdue_is_derived: OVERDUE is computed from elapsed time at read, not written by a scheduled job, so it cannot fail to fire because a cron did not run.
payout_obligation.payout_calldata: The exact ERC-20 transfer the Safe must execute is recorded at adjudication time, so a counterparty can verify what should be signed rather than trusting a later description of it. Recording calldata is not proposing or signing it — StillOS does not auto-propose Safe transactions.
payout_obligation.discharge: PAID is only written after an on-chain payout has been verified: notary_bond_slash.cjs --record-external re-reads the transaction receipt and requires a real USDC Transfer of the stated amount from the bond wallet to the disputant before it will record anything.

payout_sla.reason: Payment requires 2 of 2 Safe signatures. One key is held on the box and could be signed programmatically; the other is on a single human's phone, with no backup signer, no second human, and no on-call rotation. StillOS cannot mechanically honour a deadline that depends on one person being awake, and will not publish one it cannot honour.
payout_sla.what_is_committed_instead: The obligation is recorded durably and synchronously at adjudication time, is independently inspectable from that moment, and reports OVERDUE after the visibility threshold below. This is a guarantee that lateness is visible, not a guarantee of promptness.
payout_sla.materiality: Whether the absence of a payout SLA makes ForeSeal's Precondition 1 unsatisfied is ForeSeal's assessment to make, not StillOS's.

custody.independently_verifiable: Call getOwners() and getThreshold() on the Safe at Base mainnet. Both return the values above.
custody.classification_basis: Both owner addresses are attributable to Marcus Still from StillOS's own records (still-os-consciousness/deploy-sovereign-safe.mjs sets exactly these two owners; the box signer's private key is on the StillOS host and is used by still-os-consciousness/safe-bond-refund-propose.mjs). There is no second party. A different address is not an independent party, and this manifest does not claim otherwise.
custody.security_benefit: Real and independently checkable. Compromise of the StillOS host alone — including root on that host — cannot move the collateral, because the box holds only one of the two required signatures. This materially raises the cost of stealing the bond.
custody.counterparty_governance_benefit: None. Both keys are controlled by the same person. No independent party can compel, co-sign, or veto a payout. Multisig custody here protects the collateral from theft; it does not give a counterparty any additional assurance that an adjudicated debt will actually be paid. Those are different properties and are stated separately on purpose.
custody.what_secures_payment_instead: The obligation ledger (payout_obligation above) makes an unpaid adjudicated debt permanently visible and drops the bond out of health. That is a reputational and observability rail, not a trustless one.
custody.honest_summary: This is a self-custodied bond with hardened custody, not a trustless escrow contract. 'Slashable' here means a bonded payout obligation subject to 2-of-2 governed execution. It does not mean an instant or trustless slash, and no wording in this package should be read as claiming that.

health_semantics._added_2026_09_11: Collateral being funded does not mean every economic obligation is current. Before this revision, bond health was computed from balance + gas floor + slash-log integrity only, all of which stay green while an adjudicated unpaid debt sits outstanding.
health_semantics.healthy_requires: collateral_funded AND payable AND slash_log_intact AND available_bond > 0 AND obligation_ledger_intact AND overdue_slash_obligations == 0

bond.verify_instruction: Anyone can independently call USDC.balanceOf(wallet) on Base mainnet, and getOwners()/getThreshold() on the Safe. Do not trust this file or /notary/bond's numbers without checking the chain directly.

expected_terminal_states._note: These are the observable states the lifecycle can produce, plus StillOS's own predictions where it has one. Nothing here is a ForeSeal commitment.
expected_terminal_states.settlement: settled:true on Base, payer wallet != any StillOS-controlled address
expected_terminal_states.verdict: CONFIRMED expected by StillOS (matches an independent re-run of the same GitHub PR)
expected_terminal_states.offline_verification: signature_valid AND hash_intact AND chain_intact, computed with zero network calls to StillOS
expected_terminal_states.dispute: REJECTED or UPHELD. StillOS predicts REJECTED because the reference fact is permanently true. ForeSeal has pre-agreed neither.
expected_terminal_states.if_upheld: A durable obligation is opened in state SLASH_OWED before any signature is sought. Payment requires a human 2-of-2 Safe signature and carries no committed deadline.
